column1: # The Switch 2 leaves games 9 GB of its 12 GB (Donkey Kong Bananza's figure). The NPDM declares 48 MB of system resource, so virtual address memory is on.
# 256 MiB in front + 8 GiB heap + 256 MiB stacks + 8 GiB alias region. At 4 GiB the Chamber of Sages transition runs out of room for a 50.03 MiB address region (#3103).
# mem_map_limit on with 1 GB of room past the pool (v4): with no limit (cheemu21's L6.1, as above but without the limit) the time skip played, but in a 21-minute run the game's mapped memory grew
# to 6.77 GB (it keeps freed pages mapped while maps succeed) and the iPhone ran out of memory in Hyrule Field. The time skip needs 3.28 GB mapped; the pool leaves 2.74 GB
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time

# As Tears of the Kingdom: the terrain's height, blend and hole maps are written by the CPU into textures after they are created. Without these keys they stay zero: holes in the ground and the wrong materials
# Touch controls from cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake: the Native layout (a mobile game's layout in very transparent glass) in the Forest colours; DM_PAD_THEME=0 in env.txt gives the Classic colours
# The game submits a frame's commands behind an event its CPU signals once the frame before has left the GPU, so the GPU starts each frame with nothing queued and waits for the
# replay: with Metal encoding on its own thread a GPU-bound Hyrule Field scene went 55.3-55.8 -> 56.5-56.9 fps (Apple M4 Pro, three runs a side, interleaved)
# On the iPhone Duo the replay encodes itself instead (enc_thread_ios off): Castle Town dropped about half as many frames (34-40 fps against 24-33), Kakariko held its 40 fps,
# and the real-time shares follow (hle_nvn.c rt_share: 0.25 acquire, 0.65 replay). DM_NVN_ENC_THREAD=1 or the launcher's Encode thread turns it back on
# Screen shape (patches.py screen_shape): DM_SCREEN_ASPECT renders the iPhone Duo's 1.43:1 screen in its own shape, the display size's height from the screen's ratio
# (2560x1792 docked) and the views' vertical angle widened so 16:9's sides stay in view (more above and below); the iOS launcher offers it (Picture shape)
